title: [Android] CameraX preview is rotated 90 degrees
body: I'm using the camera package on Android after upgrading my dependencies. With camera 0.11.0+2 and camera_android_camerax 0.6.8+3, the CameraX preview is rotated by 90 degrees. camera_android uses a Texture directly for CameraPlatform.buildPreview, while camera_android_camerax applies additional preview transformations, and CameraPreview performs further Android rotation handling. I am concerned that the implementations may be applying inconsistent or duplicate corrections.

symptoms_visible: The Android CameraX preview is rotated by 90 degrees with camera 0.11.0+2 and camera_android_camerax 0.6.8+3.
N0.label: N0 rotated CameraX preview reported

symptoms_visible: The preview is still rotated on package versions containing the previously linked rotation fix, both with the regular Skia renderer and when I try enabling Impeller.
N1_x.label: N1_x duplicate closure rejected

symptoms_visible: The Pixel 1 and its API 29 emulator show an incorrectly rotated preview, while an old Samsung running API 22 displays it correctly.
On a Pixel 3a API 34 emulator, the initial preview is correct, but it becomes incorrect when I rotate the device 90 degrees to the right.
Other affected Android devices show the live CameraX preview rotated and sometimes stretched, while the captured photo itself can remain correctly oriented.
N2.label: N2 device and orientation pattern collected

symptoms_visible: A package containing the API 29 threshold change corrects the preview on several API 29 devices, but the preview can still start 90 or 180 degrees off when the app is opened in landscape.
On a naturally landscape tablet, portrait orientations can display correctly while landscape orientations remain incorrect; with auto-rotate disabled, the orientations appear inverted.
N3.label: N3 API threshold fix shown to be incomplete

symptoms_visible: Wrapping CameraPreview in a hard-coded RotatedBox can make the initial portrait preview look correct, but the preview is wrong again after the device is rotated or when another orientation is used.
N3_x.label: N3_x manual quarter-turn workaround aftermath

symptoms_visible: With the candidate plugin branch, the preview is still sideways on a Galaxy Tab, Galaxy S23, and a previously correct Pixel 7.
The incorrect preview occurs in tests using Vulkan, OpenGLES, and Skia, so changing the rendering backend alone does not restore the correct orientation.
N4.label: N4 candidate removal and renderer theory falsified

symptoms_visible: After updating to the plugin containing both preview-rotation fixes, the CameraPreview is correctly oriented on affected real devices, including a Samsung tablet and the customer's previously affected device.
N_terminal.label: N_terminal corrected preview confirmed

symptoms_visible: After removing the hard-coded RotatedBox and updating to the plugin containing both fixes, the CameraPreview remains correctly oriented through the device orientations that previously failed.
N_terminal_manual.label: N_terminal_manual workaround removed and preview corrected

solution.intent: Treat the report as a duplicate of the earlier Impeller preview-rotation issue and use a build or package containing that existing fix.
solution.concrete_example: This looks like the previously fixed Impeller preview issue; switch to the latest main branch and rerun the sample.

edges.comment: Messages c1-c4, on the original reporter's system: the issue was initially closed as a duplicate, but the reporter established that the linked fix was already included and the preview remained rotated with both Skia and attempted Impeller.

question_patterns: Does this still happen with a package containing the previously released preview fix?
Does changing between the regular renderer and Impeller change the result?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. The linked fix was already available in the versions I tested, and the issue reproduces after that fix. I see the same result with the regular Skia engine and when I try enabling Impeller.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No. The latest package containing the earlier fix displays the preview correctly on the same device.

question_patterns: Which camera_android_camerax versions are good and bad on the same device?
Can you narrow down the package-version boundary?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The preview works through camera_android_camerax 0.6.7+2 and reproduces on the versions after that.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The exact first bad patch version differs, but 0.6.7+2 is still good and the 0.6.8 series is bad.
Every CameraX package version I tested has the same rotation problem, including 0.6.7+2.

question_patterns: Can you test the same sample on another Android device and report the device and API level?
Does the problem reproduce on both the Pixel 1 and another non-Pixel device?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On my Pixel 1 running Android 29, the preview is always incorrect. Its API 29 emulator behaves exactly like the real device. An old Samsung running Android 5.1.1, API 22, works as expected.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same sample is rotated identically on both the Pixel 1 API 29 and Samsung API 22.

question_patterns: Does rotating the device change when the preview is wrong?
Can you test both landscape directions and describe the result?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On a Pixel 3a API 34 emulator, the initial view is correct. Rotating it 90 degrees to the right, with the selfie camera on the right, makes the preview incorrect; rotating to the left produces the correct preview.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The preview remains correctly oriented in portrait and both landscape directions.
The wrong landscape direction is left instead of right, but only one orientation is incorrect.

question_patterns: Do affected users see only rotation, or is the live preview also stretched?
Is the captured photo wrong too, or only the live CameraX preview?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On the other affected devices, the CameraX preview before taking the photo is rotated and stretched. The photo shown afterward is not stretched. These screenshots show the live preview and the captured-photo view.

edges.comment: Messages c2, c6, c14-c16, c19, c22 and c25. The original reporter supplied the package boundary and Pixel/Samsung/emulator results; affected participants' device and screenshot evidence is folded into the simulated user side without mixing in the separate recorded-video playback problem.

question_patterns: What is the last package version where the preview is correctly oriented?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: camera_android_camerax 0.6.7+2 is the last version that works for me; versions after it reproduce the rotated preview.

question_patterns: Can you compare the sample on another physical device and include Android API levels?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The Pixel 1 on API 29 is always wrong, including its emulator, while my old Samsung on API 22 is correct.

question_patterns: What happens when you rotate the device in each direction?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On the Pixel 3a API 34 emulator, portrait starts correctly, landscape right is wrong, and landscape left is correct.

question_patterns: Are there matching reports from other devices, and is the saved photo also distorted?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. Several affected devices show a rotated and stretched live preview, while the displayed captured photo itself is not stretched.

edges.comment: Recovery after the rejected duplicate closure, using the same reporter and folded affected-user evidence from c2-c25.

question_patterns: Please test the package containing the API-level threshold adjustment and report what changes.
Does the updated CameraX plugin correct the preview on API 29 and on devices started in landscape?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The updated plugin fixes the rotated live preview on several API 29 devices, including a Huawei and Redmi Note 7. However, starting a Pixel 5 in landscape still gives a preview that is 90 or 180 degrees off.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The updated plugin fixes every tested orientation on all affected devices, including when the app starts in landscape.
The API 29 devices are fixed, but the remaining startup-landscape failure is reproduced on a different API 34 phone.

question_patterns: Can you give exact steps that reliably reproduce the remaining rotation problem?
Does locking auto-rotate before opening the camera app affect the preview?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I can reproduce it by locking another app in landscape and then opening the camera app. The camera preview stays locked in landscape but is distorted. I also reproduce it by rotating the Pixel 5 into landscape before starting the app.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The app starts with the correct preview regardless of its initial orientation or whether auto-rotate is locked.

question_patterns: On the naturally landscape tablet, please test every device orientation with auto-rotate on and off.
Which tablet orientations display correctly, and which remain inverted?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With auto-rotate on, portrait up and portrait down are correct, but both landscape directions are incorrect. With auto-rotate off, the preview appears inverted in each orientation. I used CameraPreview and attached the four results.

edges.comment: Messages c30, c56-c67 and c75-c81. Results from multiple affected users are folded together. The API 29 package test is a measurement: the users report device outcomes, while conclusions about ImageReader, SurfaceProducer, or correction logic remain engineer-side.

solution.intent: Manually rotate and resize CameraPreview with a fixed RotatedBox quarter turn and an AspectRatio wrapper.
solution.concrete_example: Wrap CameraPreview in RotatedBox(quarterTurns: 1) and use cameraController.value.aspectRatio to make the initial preview appear upright.

edges.comment: Messages c135-c146: manual RotatedBox and aspect-ratio snippets could make one orientation look correct, but users found they failed after rotation or on other orientations and platforms. This is a persisted application-code workaround, represented by state S1b.

question_patterns: Please test the candidate plugin branch on affected real devices and report the orientation without adding manual rotation.
Does the candidate build display correctly on the tablet, phone, and both front and rear cameras?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested the candidate branch with the sample app. The preview is still incorrectly rotated on my Galaxy Tab and Galaxy S23, for both front and rear cameras. A physical Pixel 7 that was previously correct also becomes rotated by 90 degrees.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The candidate branch displays the preview correctly in every orientation on all three real devices.

question_patterns: Which rendering backend is reported in the Flutter log?
Can you compare the preview with Vulkan, forced OpenGLES, and --no-enable-impeller?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The log reports the Impeller Vulkan backend. I also tested OpenGLES and Skia with --no-enable-impeller on the Galaxy Tab, and the preview is incorrectly rotated with all three.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The preview is wrong only with Vulkan and becomes correct with both OpenGLES and Skia.
The same incorrect result occurs on Vulkan and Skia, but I could not run the OpenGLES test.

edges.comment: Messages c94-c106 and c113-c116. Affected users tested a pre-landing candidate branch and reported raw device/backend outcomes. The failed candidate showed that simply removing or replacing the old rotation correction was not the complete solution.

solution.intent: Fix CameraX preview orientation by rebuilding the preview widget whenever the orientation stream changes and by asking SurfaceProducer whether it already handles crop and rotation before applying a Flutter-side correction; then have affected users verify a build containing both changes.
solution.concrete_example: Replace the static Texture-only preview path with a widget that reacts to orientation-stream updates, and choose the corrected or uncorrected preview path from SurfaceProducer.handlesCropAndRotation() rather than an Android API-level approximation. The change was released in camera_android_camerax 0.6.14, after which affected users confirmed correct previews on real devices.
solution.inference_hint: The final diagnosis in c161 was engineer-derived: the orientation calculation could update while the preview remained a static Texture that did not rebuild, and Android API level was only an unreliable proxy for whether SurfaceProducer's backend already handled crop and rotation. These conclusions must be inferred from the cross-device, orientation-change, partial-patch, candidate-build, and backend test results rather than spoken by the user.

edges.comment: Messages c157-c171 and c182. Engineers paired and identified the two-part final fix. It landed in camera_android_camerax 0.6.14. A Samsung Tab S9 FE+ user and participant27's affected customer subsequently confirmed correct behavior on their real devices; the separate naturally landscape MicroTouch case was split for follow-up and is not chained into this resolution.

solution.intent: Remove the hard-coded application-level quarter-turn workaround and use the plugin fix that rebuilds on orientation changes and conditionally applies rotation based on SurfaceProducer crop-and-rotation handling, followed by testing on the affected device.
solution.concrete_example: Remove the RotatedBox workaround, update to camera_android_camerax 0.6.14, and rotate the real device through the previously failing orientations to confirm that CameraPreview remains upright.
solution.inference_hint: The manual quarter-turn only masks one orientation. The accepted plugin diagnosis is that orientation updates were not rebuilding the preview widget and the plugin was using API level instead of the SurfaceProducer capability to decide whether an extra correction was needed.

edges.comment: Recovery from the persisted manual-rotation workaround discussed in c135-c146. The plugin-side fix from c161-c171 replaces the workaround, and c182 records confirmation from the affected customer's device without the earlier manual correction.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify both accepted causes: the preview widget was not rebuilt when the orientation stream emitted a new device orientation, and Android API level was an unreliable proxy for whether the SurfaceProducer backend already handled crop and rotation.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected cross-device and orientation evidence, including the incomplete API 29 threshold fix, startup-in-landscape failures, and candidate tests across Vulkan, OpenGLES, and Skia.
The final fix must rebuild the preview on orientation changes and use the SurfaceProducer crop-and-rotation capability to apply a Flutter-side rotation only when needed.
Must not settle on the earlier duplicate/Impeller-only explanation or a hard-coded RotatedBox correction; both were falsified by the thread's device and orientation tests.
Must keep rotated recorded-video playback and the separate naturally landscape MicroTouch behavior out of this diagnostic chain.
Must ask an affected user to verify a build containing both preview fixes on a real device before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Flutter application developer who can compare package implementations, pin or override package versions, run emulators and physical-device tests, switch rendering backends, and test plugin branches; additional affected developers and device operators are folded into the user side.
persona_hint.communication_style: Technical, responsive, and evidence-driven. Provides exact package versions, devices, API levels, orientation steps, screenshots, and backend logs, and distinguishes live CameraPreview behavior from captured-image or recorded-video playback.
